additional_concerns: The combined substantive-performance reading is plausible from paragraphs 10 and 11, but the excerpts do not define effective supervision or a complete satisfaction standard. Retained authority alone does not establish performance; neither does every incident automatically establish failure.

Actual accountability arrangements, supervision, operational performance, record accuracy, incident duration, remediation and the assessment period are absent. Missing facts must remain unresolved rather than produce a false answer.

Paragraph 14 distinguishes confirmation from demonstration upon SFC request and specifies SFC satisfaction. Footnote 5 supplies minimum content; its apparently unqualified wording must be read with the parent provision while preserving the stated rival reading. Neither demonstration nor SFC satisfaction should silently become paragraph 10's substantive test.

Paragraphs 15 and 16 separately condition third-party audit or verification and satisfactory legal opinion on SFC request. Absence of a request does not suspend underlying responsibility or proper-record duties; obtaining either item does not itself prove substantive fulfillment.

Intermediary paragraphs 17–18 have their own actor and activity conditions, due-diligence obligations and reference to Appendix Parts A and B. They do not automatically supply a Product Provider supervision standard. Those Appendix materials are absent.

The outsourcing entry's exceptions field describes preservation of responsibility, not an exemption. The source does not require personal performance of every task or reservation of every operational decision.
